newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria plans new foreign investment incentives.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria plans new foreign investment incentives.

text.p: Bulgaria's foreign investment agency plans to propose tax breaks and other incentives aimed at boosting foreign investment in the crisis-torn country, the agency's new director, Ilian Vasilev, said on Friday.
"The agency is going to draft a long-term programme for changes in Bulgaria's foreign investment policy and plan immediate promotion of investment opportunities," Vasilev told a news conference.
The agency aims to make Bulgaria's arcane and inconsistently applied foreign investment legislation clear and transparent, said Vasilev.
Proposed changes would include tax breaks and other investment incentives, which could be approved by the caretaker cabinet in power until after April 19 elections, said Vasilev.
Foreign investment for the seven years of transition since the end of communist rule totals $831 million, the lowest in the region.
Investment in 1996 totalled $302 million, of which the biggest investment was the acquisition by a Dutch firm of a majority stake in Bulgarian cornstarch producer Tzaramil from Belgium's Amylum.
Germany, traditionally the biggest investor in Bulgaria, ranked second last year with $43 million and Britain was third with $32 million.
Foreign investment is expected to rise sharply this year as the cash-strapped country relies on external support and privatisation proceeds for $1 billion of foreign debt payments due this year.
The interim cabinet hopes to sell 16 major state companies by end-March.
